## About

These Python (Jupyter) cells have `panzoom: true`, next to the document's
`lightbox: true`. panzoom takes every image lightbox would, except where a
case asks for lightbox. The [lightbox version](j-jupyter-lightbox.html) has
the same cases without panzoom. Compare each case with the same number
there. The knitr equivalent is the R [global panzoom
version](c-panzoom-auto.html).

```yaml
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom: true
lightbox: true
```

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown
on the page; the **Code** button at the top shows the full source.

The cases below share this setup:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
```

## 1. Figure with a caption {#c1 expect-open="panzoom"}

A Python figure with a caption. It opens in panzoom.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "A sine wave."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## 2. Plot without a caption {#c2 expect-open="panzoom"}

A plot without a caption. It opens in panzoom.

```{python}
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## 3. Subfigures {#c3 expect-open="panzoom"}

Two subfigures from one cell. They open in panzoom as a two-image gallery.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pair
#| fig-cap: "Two waves."
#| fig-subcap: ["Sine", "Cosine"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(2 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 4. `lightbox:` options {#c4 expect-open="glightbox"}

Two cells with `lightbox:` options for a group and a description. Asking for
lightbox keeps them out of panzoom, as with knitr (cases 6 and 7 of the R
[global panzoom version](c-panzoom-auto.html)). With Jupyter, lightbox
ignores the options themselves, so each opens in lightbox on its own,
without the group or description.

```{python}
#| lightbox:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Ignored by lightbox with Jupyter."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 5. `lightbox: false` {#c5 expect-open="nothing"}

A cell with `lightbox: false`. panzoom leaves an explicit lightbox setting
alone, so clicking it does nothing.

```{python}
#| lightbox: false

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 6. `panzoom: true` on a cell {#c6 expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with `panzoom: true`. It opens in panzoom, ahead of the document's
`lightbox: true`.

```{python}
#| panzoom: true

plt.plot(x, np.cos(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 7. Markdown image {#c7 expect-open="panzoom"}

A markdown image alone in a paragraph. It opens in panzoom.

```{.markdown .show-source}
![Chilmark.](../../images/mv-0.jpg)
```

## 8. `.nolightbox` {#c8 expect-open="nothing"}

A markdown image with `.nolightbox`. panzoom only takes images lightbox
would, so clicking it does nothing.

```{.markdown .show-source}
![Opted out.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){.nolightbox}
```
